120: The easiest pitfall to overlook: no permission protection by default
121: By default Pi does not pop up a confirmation before deleting files or running commands, the way some desktop agents do. It directly inherits the file, network, credential and system permissions of the process that started it.
122: That is not a hidden bug, though; the official home page states “No permission popups” plainly.
123: For people comfortable with a terminal that means YOLO mode, so the task is not interrupted constantly.
124: But for a beginner, one loosely written prompt really can make the agent do damage, such as wiping your C drive...
125: If you are new to it, pay attention to the following:
126: Start in an empty directory; do not open the desktop, documents or your whole home directory straight away;
127: When reading code, lock it read-only with --tools read,grep,find,ls;
128: Do not let the model read ~/.pi/agent/auth.json, .env or other credential files;
129: Review the source of third-party Packages and Extensions before installing;
130: If it really must run automatically for a long time, put it in Docker, OpenShell or another sandbox.
131: The official documentation offers several isolation options. The most convenient is to put the whole of Pi into Docker.
132: Note that a mounted working directory can still write back to the host; also mounting the host's ~/.pi/agent exposes the authentication and session files to the container.

136: If you just want to download a product, sign in and use it reliably behind safety rails, Pi is not necessarily the least hassle. It deliberately leaves out some things “that should be there once installed”, and much has to be configured yourself.
137: People already using several models, with a pile of Skills, who want to wire an agent into scripts or products and have a basic judgement about terminals and permissions will feel its value more easily. Especially those running a one-person company or working independently.
138: Of course, the more freedom there is, the more you have to guard the security side yourself.
